key_findings.title: Stereo‑supervised self‑supervision eliminates metric ground‑truth dependence
key_findings.source: On the Synergies between Machine Learning and Binocular Stereo for Depth Estimation from Images: a Survey
key_findings.summary: View‑synthesis losses (photometric, left‑right consistency, minimum reprojection) allow monocular networks to learn depth without metric labels, removing scale ambiguity and achieving competitive KITTI results (e.g., MonoDepth2 AbsRel 0.106).

key_findings.title: Distillation from high‑performance stereo teachers narrows the gap to fully supervised methods
key_findings.source: On the Synergies between Machine Learning and Binocular Stereo for Depth Estimation from Images: a Survey
key_findings.summary: Cross‑domain and MonoResMatch pipelines generate dense pseudo‑labels from stereo nets, providing richer supervision than pure view synthesis and improving accuracy on outdoor benchmarks.

key_findings.title: Motion‑aware cost volumes improve depth in dynamic scenes
key_findings.source: Manydepth2: Motion-Aware Self-Supervised Monocular Depth Estimation in Dynamic Scenes
key_findings.summary: By constructing a pseudo‑static reference frame with optical flow and integrating it into a motion‑aware volume, Manydepth2 reduces KITTI AbsRel to 0.091 and gains ~15 % on Cityscapes, evidencing the importance of explicit dynamic handling.

key_findings.title: Depth factorization with transformer‑based scale regression boosts indoor performance
key_findings.source: MonoIndoor++: Towards Better Practice of Self-Supervised Monocular Depth Estimation for Indoor Environments
key_findings.summary: Separating global scale (learned via a transformer) from relative depth yields a 2.8 % absolute‑relative error reduction on NYUv2 and tighter pose errors on EuRoC, addressing the scale‑ambiguity problem in indoor video.

key_findings.title: Lightweight encoder‑decoder designs enable real‑time inference at the cost of accuracy
key_findings.source: On the Synergies between Machine Learning and Binocular Stereo for Depth Estimation from Images: a Survey
key_findings.summary: Models such as PyDNet and MADNet‑style adaptations demonstrate monocular depth on CPUs/embedded devices, but exhibit higher errors than high‑resolution supervised counterparts, highlighting the accuracy‑efficiency trade‑off.

synthesis: Between 2023 and 2025 monocular depth estimation has converged on self‑supervised view‑synthesis training, largely driven by stereo‑supervised cues that remove the need for metric ground truth and alleviate scale ambiguity. Distillation from strong stereo teachers further refines supervision, narrowing the performance gap to fully supervised methods. Recent work has extended this paradigm to address two persistent challenges: dynamic scenes and indoor environments. Motion‑aware cost volumes, built from pseudo‑static frames derived via optical flow, substantially improve robustness to moving objects, while transformer‑based scale regression and depth factorisation explicitly resolve the global scale problem endemic to indoor video, yielding state‑of‑the‑art results on NYUv2 and EuRoC. Concurrently, lightweight encoder‑decoder architectures demonstrate that real‑time deployment on edge devices is feasible, though at a measurable accuracy penalty. Despite these advances, generalization across domains, handling of illumination changes, and the computational burden of high‑resolution models remain open research gaps that future studies must address.
